items.text: Deep dive into BAS chain confirms the exact pattern to replicate. Each provider implements 4 methods: Type(), IsAvailable(ctx), Execute(ctx, req), Model(). Chain tries providers in order with a critical rule: ErrInsufficientCredits stops fallback immediately (don't fall through to free tier when user is out of credits), all other errors continue to next provider. Availability caching uses different TTLs per tier: BYOK 5min, Vrooli 30sec, Dev one-time check. Factory pattern creates per-request clients injecting user credentials (BYOK key, LPBS auth token) while sharing the chain instance. LPBS usage reporting is async with 3-attempt exponential backoff and operation_id for idempotency.

Complete audio API contracts documented. Whisper STT: POST multipart audio → JSON {text}; also WebSocket streaming with partial/final/segment-final events. Kokoro TTS: POST JSON {input, voice, speed, response_format} → raw audio bytes; also has /voices list and per-eventId caching. Ollama summarization: POST /api/chat with system prompt for light/moderate/heavy levels → JSON {message.content}. All three currently connect directly to localhost with no routing, no BYOK, no credit metering.

LPBS credit system is more sophisticated than expected. Non-streaming uses atomic ReserveAndCharge with reconciliation (refund if overestimated, top-up if underestimated). Streaming uses a three-phase reservation system: ReserveCredits → Stream → FinalizeReservation, with 10-minute auto-expiry on pending reservations. This reservation infrastructure can be reused for audio without major changes — the key extension is adding audio-specific pricing models (per-second or per-byte rather than per-token).

items.context: LPBS currently prices by token count (input/output tokens per 1M). Audio capabilities don't have tokens — STT processes audio duration, TTS produces audio duration, summarization uses tokens. Need to decide the pricing unit for audio operations.

options.label: Per-second pricing for STT/TTS, per-token for summarization
options.rationale: Most natural fit: STT cost scales with audio length, TTS cost scales with output length. Summarization already fits the token model. External APIs (Deepgram, ElevenLabs) price this way. Requires new LPBS pricing fields for audio duration.

options.label: Flat per-operation credits (like BAS execution runs)
options.rationale: Simplest: 1 credit per transcription, 2 credits per synthesis, 1 credit per summary. No duration/size tracking needed. BAS already uses this for non-AI operations. But doesn't scale fairly — a 5-second transcription costs the same as a 5-minute one.

options.label: Tiered buckets (small/medium/large)
options.rationale: Middle ground: charge 1/2/4 credits based on audio length brackets (e.g., <30s, 30s-5m, >5m). Coarser than per-second but fairer than flat. Simpler LPBS changes than per-second.

items.topic: WebSocket STT streaming through provider chain
items.context: Whisper STT has two modes: HTTP batch (send complete audio, get transcript) and WebSocket streaming (real-time partial transcripts). The provider chain pattern works naturally for HTTP batch requests. WebSocket streaming is more complex — external/LPBS providers may not support streaming, or may have different WebSocket protocols.

options.label: Route only HTTP batch through provider chain; streaming stays local-only
options.rationale: Simplest approach. Streaming STT is latency-sensitive and protocol-specific — routing it through a provider chain adds complexity for little benefit. Local Whisper streaming already works well. BYOK/LPBS users can still use HTTP batch transcription.

options.label: Route both HTTP and WebSocket through provider chain
options.rationale: Full feature parity across tiers. Provider interface would need a StreamTranscribe method alongside Transcribe. More complex but ensures users without local Whisper can still get streaming. Would require LPBS to proxy WebSocket connections.

items.topic: Configuration schema: per-caller vs. per-instance routing preferences
items.context: Need to define how callers (web-console, swarm-manager, agent-manager) specify their preferred provider routing. BAS uses per-instance env vars (BAS_AI_ENABLE_BYOK, etc.) and per-request credentials (BYOK key, LPBS token). Audio-tools needs a similar system but serving multiple callers.

options.label: Per-instance defaults + per-request caller overrides
options.rationale: Audio-tools has instance-level defaults (env vars for enable flags, URLs). Each API request includes optional caller credentials (BYOK key, LPBS token) that determine which tiers are available for that request. Matches BAS pattern exactly. Callers don't need to specify routing — the chain resolves it based on what credentials are present.

options.label: Per-capability routing configuration
options.rationale: Callers can specify preferred provider per-capability: 'use local Whisper but LPBS for TTS'. More flexible but adds configuration complexity. Could be a JSON config body or query params on each request.

options.label: Caller registration with stored preferences
options.rationale: Each caller registers with audio-tools and stores their routing preferences. Audio-tools looks up caller config on each request by caller ID. Most flexible but adds state management and a registration flow.

items.text: Per-capability typed provider interfaces for audio-tools would look like: STTProvider { Type(), IsAvailable(ctx), Transcribe(ctx, audio []byte, opts STTOpts) (STTResult, error) }; TTSProvider { Type(), IsAvailable(ctx), Synthesize(ctx, req TTSRequest) ([]byte, error) }; SummarizeProvider { Type(), IsAvailable(ctx), Summarize(ctx, text string, level string) (string, error) }. Each gets its own chain (STTChain, TTSChain, SummarizeChain) following the BYOK → Vrooli → Local fallback order.

LPBS gateway extension requirements for full audio support (d2 from round 1 selected B): (1) POST /api/v1/ai/transcribe — accepts multipart audio upload, proxies to cloud Whisper/Deepgram, charges credits based on audio duration; (2) POST /api/v1/ai/synthesize — accepts JSON text+voice, proxies to cloud TTS, returns audio bytes, charges credits based on output duration; (3) POST /api/v1/ai/summarize — can reuse existing /ai/chat endpoint with operation metadata. This is a significant LPBS scope expansion requiring its own execution item.
